Edge & on-device inference (Simon Willison's stateless-MCP reversal turns on exactly this axis — a shell with internet access needs a strong model, while MCP tools are simple enough for laptop-sized local models to drive; a Show HN runs Kimi K3 in 29 GB of RAM at 0.50 tok/s, and ollama's own description remains a live model-support ranking with Kimi-K2.6 and GLM-5.2 ahead of Western open weights)

MCP adoption (a 1,847-server census finds 52% abandoned, 31% lightly maintained and only 17% production-grade, median server at 6 lifetime commits last touched 142 days ago; 97M monthly SDK downloads against 37,000–95,000 low-signal listings; the stateless revision starts breaking sessions in practice)

Agent execution control (CAGE proves certifying the categorical and numerical channels of a tool return separately does not compose; Cloudflare previews human-out-of-the-loop lifecycle and agent access controls; agentgateway named as the enterprise chokepoint where model access, tool calls and MCP servers get one policy)

Agent memory (a LightMem reproduction shows retriever choice dominates memory architecture and oracle evaluation finds memory construction discards answer-relevant information; Zero-Mem cuts memory-operation time 57.6% with no LLM call outside final QA; agents recall a stated preference yet fail to act on it)

MCP adoption & the 2026-07-28 spec (a Swiss private bank writes 'standards such as the Model Context Protocol' into a job description as a delivery requirement; Snowflake ships the enforcement point at the warehouse boundary rather than the protocol; a 25-year SAP integrator benchmarks MCP against RFC/PI-PO/BTP)

Context engineering (long-horizon execution reframed as task-state management rather than a context problem — a manager picks the subtask, a fresh-context executor runs it, a read-only auditor verifies the environment before the next round, lifting Qwen 3.7-Plus 51.8% → 80.7% on WeaveBench)

Context engineering (the man who coined the term now says it is the wrong frame — Dex Horthy pushes past context engineering to harness and loop engineering, the durable leverage being the wrapper around the model rather than the prompt; and the failure mode gets named precisely on LinkedIn, an explicit guardrail surviving until the conversation grows long enough that summarisation renders it vague)
